subject: Mid-contract uplift options and co-term amendment
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stellarapps.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Imran Khan <imran.k@stellarapps.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity bump / pricing question

Hi Priyom,

Quick note — we just saw a 2.5x spike in API usage after last week's product launch. The spike is sustained (not a one-off) and we need an interim uplift to avoid throttling while we finalize a larger renewal.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide a temporary committed uplift for the remainder of our current contract term (through Feb 2028) with a pathway to annualize at renewal? We care about:
- unit price for the additional committed tokens / GPU-hours
- co-terming to align the uplift to our Feb renewal
- whether we can split the uplift across two invoices (Sept + Nov) for budget reasons

I can share an internal forecast if helpful. Looping Imran for procurement visibility.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Head of Platform, StellarApps
[Attachment: customer-forecast-q4.csv (CSV stub)]

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stellarapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump / pricing question

Claire — thanks for the heads-up and congrats on the launch traction. We can support a mid-contract uplift; below are two practical paths that balance speed vs economics.

Option 1 — Temporary uplift (fast):
- Term: Oct 2027  Feb 2028 (5 months)
- Structure: one-sided committed uplift (Redwood reserves capacity)
- Commercial: modest blended discount to on-demand; no co-term amendment required
- Invoicing: we can accommodate a split payment schedule as a one-off (your Sept + Nov split) if procurement needs it

Option 2 — Bridge-to-renew (recommended if you want better unit price):
- Term: amend and annualize uplift effective Sept 2027 with co-term to Feb 2028 (true-up at co-term)
- Commercial: better unit economics (materially lower than temporary uplift) but requires signed amendment and PO
- Timing: legal & procurement alignment needed; we can fast-track minimal review in 35 business days with approvals lane

To scope a priced MOP I need: a 6-week forecast (ballpark ok), preferred invoicing approach, and the procurement signer. I attached the Redwood ratecard (v2) and a short MOP draft for internal review.

Marissa — can you produce two concrete $ scenarios (Option 1 vs Option 2) based on +150M tokens/month uplift?
Jonas / Karthik — any capacity or SLA banding we should call out?

I will turn around a priced amendment by EOD tomorrow if Claire can share the forecast.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (PDF)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stellarapps.com>, Imran Khan <imran.k@stellarapps.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift options  draft numbers

Team  I ran two quick scenarios and put the arithmetic into the MOP draft (attached). Assumptions: baseline committed = 100M tokens/month, observed = ~250M tokens/month after launch, target uplift = +150M tokens/month.

Scenario A (Temporary uplift):
- OctFeb (5 months) +150M tokens/month at ~12% blended discount to on-demand
- Total uplift spend: $225,000 (example calc in MOP)
- Invoicing: we can split Sept 50% / Nov 50% as an accounting exception
- Pros: fastest to get capacity reserved
- Cons: less favorable unit economics; uplift sunsets at term

Scenario B (Bridge-to-renew / co-term amend):
- Annualize +150M tokens/month effective Sept; convert into committed units with a true-up at Feb co-term
- Effective unit price: ~22% lower than on-demand (better long-term economics)
- Requirements: signed amendment, PO, legal review (35 business days)
- Pros: best price and predictable floor for your product team
- Cons: requires procurement/legal alignment now

Jonas  please confirm there is capacity headroom to reserve +150M tokens/month for StellarApps in our west region.
Karthik  please confirm priority banding (SLA) we commit to for the uplifted capacity.

If Claire confirms Scenario B we will produce a priced amendment + procurement checklist (PO number, billing code, contact list) for Imran/Anika.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: stellar-uplift-mop-draft-20270914.docx (DOCX)]

- target uplift: +150M tokens/month
- invoicing: single PO preferred, but procurement can accept a split if Redwood requires it
- primary signer: Imran Khan (Procurement); legal reviewer: Anika Rao (in-house legal)
